name: Storage
overview: Watch the disks and shares Jellyfin uses.
description: Storage watches every disk and share Jellyfin uses. It warns when one fills up or starts failing, protects your library when one goes missing, remounts it, and formats new disks.

versions.changelog:
## Added
- The Storage tab lists each disk and share your libraries use, with its mount state, its space, and the libraries on it
- A filter for disks no library uses, and a dialog with each disk's space, alerts, libraries, and folders
- The Check storage task records disks that go missing, become unresponsive, come back, or pass the Storage low or Storage full alert in the activity log
- Library scans are blocked while a disk they would scan is missing, and real-time monitoring ignores its folders
- All also lists disks with no file system as Unformatted, with their model and size, on Linux, macOS, and Windows when Jellyfin runs as an administrator
- Each disk's SMART health, with its temperature, power-on time, and wear where it reports them, and a Disk failing entry in the activity log when one starts failing
- A missing disk is mounted again at each check, a share through NetFS on macOS and WNetAddConnection2 on Windows, and an fstab entry through systemd on Linux, with Disk remounted and Disk not remounted entries in the activity log
- An unformatted disk's dialog formats it with a name and file system, mounts it where it stays mounted, and can add it to a library, after the name is typed to confirm. Linux uses udisks2, Windows the Storage Management API, and macOS diskutil
- Disks holding Jellyfin's own folders, such as its cache, metadata, and transcodes, count as used by Jellyfin
- Library folders Jellyfin cannot write to are flagged, and exFAT and NTFS disks formatted on Linux mount owned by Jellyfin's user
- A mounted disk's dialog makes a folder at the top of the disk and can add it to a library in one step
- A share's dialog sets the address it is remounted from, for a share the plugin never saw mounted
- On Linux, disks that hold data but are not mounted are listed with what's on them, and can be erased and formatted once their device name is typed
- Each disk is tagged Local, External, Network, or System, with External found from USB, Thunderbolt, and removable media on each OS
- Disk health alerts for a failing disk, a disk running too hot, and a worn out SSD, each recorded once in the activity log and set on the Settings tab
- The Storage tab leads with a banner of what needs a look and cards adding up the space of every disk in use
- Each disk can override the Storage low and Storage full alerts in its dialog
- The Settings tab sets the Storage low and Storage full alerts, when scans are blocked, whether missing disks are remounted, and whether monitoring is paused
